headline: Microsoft tests Remote Lock for lost or stolen Windows PCs
summary: Microsoft is testing a new Remote Lock feature, enabled through Intune, that lets enterprise IT administrators remotely lock a lost, stolen or compromised Windows device without wiping its data. The feature blocks normal sign-ins while preserving data on the device.

claims.statement: Microsoft is testing a feature letting enterprise IT administrators remotely lock lost or stolen Windows devices without wiping them.

sources.quote: Microsoft is testing a new feature that lets enterprise IT administrators remotely lock stolen or lost Windows devices without wiping them.

claims.statement: The Intune-enabled feature lets admins remotely lock down any compromised Windows device.

sources.quote: The Intune-enabled feature will allow admins to remotely lock down any compromised Windows device.

claims.statement: The feature blocks normal sign-ins without wiping data, while a separate test build drops Offline Maps settings.

sources.quote: Intune feature blocks normal sign-ins without wiping data, while another test build drops Offline Maps settings
